Rolandic mu rhythms (high-frequency alpha and low-frequency beta) are related to sympathetic component of autoregulation of heart rate in healthy humans.

Rolandic low frequency beta rhythms are involved in somatomotion control, and that this activity is related to sympathetic activity.

Rolandic mu rhythms, which are supposed to reflect activity of somatomator cortex, are associated with activity of sympathetic component in ANS.

Rolandic mu rhythms, which are a putative neural mechanism of inter-hemispheric synchronization in somatomotor cortex, are related to activity regulating heart rate.
